messages:
chris: Heads-up — after the calico upgrade in ashburn GPU pool we're seeing huge p99 east-west latency spikes and RDMA falling back to TCP for training jobs. Packet loss + icmp6 unreachable logs from apps. NDP neighbor cache shows pod v6 addresses mapping to the wrong MACs. Anyone seen this pattern?

jaspreet: Can you paste `ip -6 neigh` + `ip -6 route` for an affected node and `ethtool -k` for the host interface? Also which calico IPPool settings got applied for v6?

chris: Here are snippets from node-gpu-12 (redacted):
```
# ip -6 neigh
fe80::1aa:bbff:fecc:ddff dev ens1 lladdr aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff STALE
fd00:10::42 dev cali123 lladdr 11:22:33:44:55:66 REACHABLE
fd00:10::42 dev ens1 lladdr aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff STALE

# ip -6 route show table main
fd00:10::/64 dev cali123 mtu 1450 proto kernel scope link
fd00:20::/64 dev ens1 mtu 9000 proto kernel scope link

# dmesg | grep rdma
rdma: cm_id create failed: -113
rdma: fallback to TCP
```

chris: We have duplicate entries: same pod IP learned on cali and the host iface (ens1) with different MACs. Flaps when pods move or when kernel neighbor refresh runs.

alex: Sounds like NDP proxy/mis-proxy + SR-IOV VF MAC learning collision. If calico is in ipip/vxlan encapsulation mode for v6 and we also have route-based SR-IOV with MAC learning, the fabric will advertise both and TORs can pick the wrong one. Kube-proxy IPVS + conntrack for v6 can make it worse.

chris: I flushed the neighbor table (`ip -6 neigh flush all`) and it temporarily fixed comms, but wrong entries reappeared within ~30s.

netops: We have metalLB EVPN announcing /128 v6 service IPs from TORs. There's a VRF mismatch on a subset of switches in ashburn that causes the v6 /128 to be advertised from the host-side MAC instead of the calico tunnel MAC. That explains the wrong MAC.

maria: Also check calico pool flags — if `natOutgoing=true` was copied from v4 into the v6 pool during the upgrade then kernel may be doing unexpected NDP proxying. For v6 we should normally have `natOutgoing=false` and encapsulation off for nodes on same L2.

alex: MTU mismatch looks bad too: host interface mtu 9000 but calico tunnel shows mtu 1450. RDMA expects large MTU; when packets fragment/fail you get CM errors and fallback to TCP. This is a PMTU/fragmentation blackhole for heavy east-west RDMA traffic.

chris: Confirmed. GPU nodes are SR-IOV with 9000, calico tunnel default is 1450. We accidentally applied an ipPool template that set ipipMode=Always and natOutgoing=true for the v6 pool during the roll.

jaspreet: Quick mitigations to try in order:
1) Patch calico IPPool for v6: set `ipipMode: Never` (or encapsulation: None) and `natOutgoing: false` for that pool.
2) Restart kube-proxy on a small canary set of nodes.
3) Clear neighbor table after change: `ip -6 neigh flush all` and `sysctl -w net.ipv6.neigh.default.gc_thresh2=2048` (temporarily raise) to avoid immediate re-flap.
4) If encapsulation is needed, align MTU across host+encap (but prefer disabling encap for GPU node group).

chris: I'll apply the IPPool patch to ashburn GPU nodes (canary first) and restart kube-proxy on two nodes. Also will scale some large jobs out of that AZ to reduce impact.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 — "ashburn: IPv6 NDP proxy + MTU mismatch causing RDMA fallback on GPU pool". Pagering on-call.

netops: Rolling calico ipPool patch in ashburn now (v6 natOutgoing -> false, ipipMode -> Never) on the GPU node label set. If we still see wrong MACs after the change it's likely the EVPN artifacts on TORs — will coordinate a BGP withdraw.

alex: For long term: switch GPU pool to route-based (no encapsulation) with host-local routes advertised by BGP/EVPN, ensure SR-IOV VF MAC learning is isolated, and add an NDP proxy reconciliation job in netops to detect duplicate advertisements.

chris: After the patch I see neighbor entries stabilizing and RDMA errors reduced on canary nodes. Latency p99 down from ~1.2s to ~120ms for training interconnect. Will keep monitoring for an hour and then roll to the rest of the pool. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: Great. Keep notes for postmortem and include the IPPool template diff so we don't accidentally copy v4 NAT flags into v6 in future upgrades. :eyes:
